newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US Feb durables orders rise 1.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US Feb durables orders rise 1.5 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. experts after the Commerce Department said durable goods orders rose 1.5 percent in February compared to an upwardly revised 4.1 percent rise in January.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 0.4-percent decline in orders for the month.
DAVID SLOAN, SENIOR ECONOMIST, I.D.E.A. INC: "I think the numbers are definitely much stronger than expected. What's surprising is how broad based the increase was."
Sloan was speaking on Reuters Financial Television.

KEVIN FLANAGAN, VICE PRESIDENT AND AN ECONOMIST, DEAN WITTER REYNOLDS INC: "You had a strong report here ... much stronger than expected ... and this is going to continue to add to this defensive sentiment following the (Federal Reserve's) action yesterday. It continues to show that there is forward momentum in the economic setting.
"If you were expecting to see a (U.S. Treasury) relief rally today or tomorrow, figures such as this will put an end to that thought process rather quickly," Flanagan added.
HUGH JOHNSON, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, FIRST ALBANY CORP:

"Non-defense capital goods is a little bit strong and if you're looking for something that's a market mover that could certainly be one ... This means that not only is the economy strong, but these numbers seem to tell you that the economy will remain strong, and that will stir up all those worries that the Fed will have to raise (interest rates) further.
"But these are historically very volatile numbers from month to month and next month you could have it washed out," Johnson added.
SALLY KLEINMAN, ECONOMIST, CHASE SECURITIES INC:

"Tremendously strong. Good activity in almost every sector with the exception of aircraft and we're not worried about (that sector). As we know, it's doing very well. This leads to activity in other areas of the economy; order books are bulging and manufacturers should step up production."
FRED LEVIN, CHIEF ECONOMIST, EASTBRIDGE CAPITAL INC: "The maunfacturing sector is really picking up."

Levin continued: "We are going to see a very strong increase in industrial production due to strong autos. The chances of a May tightening are increasing every day with hawkish statements by the Fed and now these orders figures."
ROBERT MCGEE, SENIOR ECONOMIST, TOKAI BANK LTD:

"This leading indicator is saying the economy has got plenty of strength. It sort of validates the Fed's feeling the economy is likely to overheat if they don't exercise a little restraint. The odds are they will do another (rate hike) in May unless something surprising happens to stop them."
CHRIS IGGO, CHIEF ECONOMIST, BZW SECURITIES INC:

"The report was higher than expected, but you have to remember that durable goods is a very volatile series and difficult to forecast ... Transportation is probably one of the most volatile components of the report.
"New orders for industrial goods and shipments of goods (were) very strong, suggesting that the economy will continue to grow quickly for the foreseable future.

"The economy is growing too quickly for the Fed's comfort level and there is a concern that inflation will start to pick up if some restraint is not seen in economic growth and that is what the Fed is trying to bring about."
(( -- N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1660 ))
